# Remote Control Agent v0.1.48 — detached owner-approved upgrades

## Changes

- Add an explicitly owner-approved, detached upgrade entrypoint for Linux x64/ARM64 (including WSL2): `rca upgrade --unattended` dispatches a short-lived same-user systemd task rather than terminating its own managed Shell.
- Add a Windows x64 non-interactive upgrade path through a demand-start-only, limited same-user Scheduled Task using the existing verified official bootstrap; original local one-click installation and interactive upgrade prompts remain unchanged.
- Use the existing Agent engine's atomic operation freeze and busy-Shell/Session detection before upgrade. Windows permanent mode uses a private named pipe to freeze admission, with a mandatory second freeze check immediately before replacing the old Task; a missing or busy pipe fails closed.
- Reuse existing package hashes, signed device ID, receipt continuity, session management and rollback. No automatic updater, special MCP upgrade endpoint, alternate deployment, new pairing protocol or new credentials.

## Owner-controlled Release boundary

This note accompanies a **draft Release-pin PR only**. No Agent Release or Worker deployment may be inferred from CI or Draft PR creation. Do not merge the pin to main without separate, explicit production publication authorization: the existing `Publish pinned Agent Release` workflow will automatically publish immutable v0.1.48 assets when the single manifest is merged.

A further reviewed Worker installer pin and protected Worker production deployment are separate actions requiring their own authorization. Physical paired-device upgrades, signed WSS reconnection, unchanged device ID and old receipt verification, and rollback are **Not performed** at candidate stage. A currently installed Agent lacking this new safe detached entrypoint cannot have the original local-TTY/operation-freeze checks silently bypassed. An owner-approved first transition is required; Windows v0.1.47 does not provide the new verified freeze IPC. Ordinary one-click interactive updates remain supported. macOS permanent support stays independent of this three-platform Release (Spec #657).
